html:
The Lil'wat are a St'at'imc, or Lillooet, people of the southern Coast Mountains of British Columbia, centred on Mount Currie near Pemberton. They speak St'at'imcets, an Interior Salish language.

They lived by salmon fishing in the Lillooet River system, hunting mountain goats and deer and gathering berries and roots, and traded across the mountains with the Squamish on the coast and the Nlaka'pamux in the interior. The Douglas Trail of the 1858 Fraser Canyon gold rush ran through their land. In 1911 the St'at'imc chiefs signed the Declaration of the Lillooet Tribe, asserting their title to the land. The Lil'wat Nation today runs one of the most populous reserves in Canada.
